findings.title: Overridable exception traceback metadata bypasses the safe diagnostic projection
findings.requirement_violated: consumer_line must be an actual integer caller line or null; diagnostic must not persist arbitrary exception-controlled strings, paths or private payloads.
findings.mechanism: error.__traceback__ performs subclass attribute/property lookup. A RuntimeError subclass can return SimpleNamespace(tb_lineno=private_string). The newly added code passes that string verbatim to the real checkpoint under consumer_line; the sanitizer only protects exceptions, not this field. It also accepts arbitrary nested JSON-compatible content, so the new metadata field is not intrinsically bounded.
findings.reproducer: commands/reproducer-corrected contains exact argv. Raise HostileTraceback with a __traceback__ property returning SimpleNamespace(tb_lineno="PUBLIC_SYNTHETIC_PRIVATE_TRACEBACK_LINE"); execute the actual extracted handler and full unchanged finally with resource doubles and the actual checkpoint writer.
findings.risk_boundary: Confirmed diagnostic-content/schema violation for a hostile exception subclass, not an observed real-secret disclosure, network exfiltration or authorization bypass. An arbitrary exception is already running in-process Python; this finding concerns the expressly safe persisted projection only.
findings.remedy: Read the real built-in traceback descriptor directly, e.g. BaseException.__traceback__.__get__(error, type(error)), rather than dispatching to the exception override; retain only its integer outer tb_lineno or null. Preserve the existing bare raise, uncertainty assignments and finally. Add one regression using this overridden property to the existing SOURCE test; require marker absence and actual integer caller line. No helper/framework, runtime fix, wider grant or third harness is needed.
findings.regression_gap: The nine passing cases exercise hostile __str__/__repr__, public context, cancellation, close error and a primary-only checkpoint error, but no hostile override at the newly introduced __traceback__/consumer_line boundary.

tree=ast.parse(Path(owner.__file__).read_bytes())
consumer=next(n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n,ast.FunctionDef) and n.name=="test_contract_method_real_native_pg_owner_receipts_check_inbox")
run=next(n for n in consumer.body if isinstance(n,ast.AsyncFunctionDef) and n.name=="run")
original=next(n for n in run.body if isinstance(n,ast.Try) and n.finalbody)
writer=next(n for n in consumer.body if isinstance(n,ast.FunctionDef) and n.name=="checkpoint")
probe=ast.parse("async def probe():\n try:\n  await fail()\n except BaseException:\n  pass\n finally:\n  pass\n")
statement=probe.body[0].body[0]
statement.handlers,statement.finalbody=original.handlers,original.finalbody
marker="PUBLIC_SYNTHETIC_PRIVATE_TRACEBACK_LINE"
class HostileTraceback(RuntimeError):
    @property
    def __traceback__(self):
        return SimpleNamespace(tb_lineno=marker)
primary=HostileTraceback("opaque")
async def fail():
    raise primary
proof={}

exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[writer],type_ignores=[]),owner.__file__,"exec"),scope)
